title: Ang 323–339: Kabir in Gauri
hookLine: the weaver's many Gauri hymns, including the caste question on ang 324
tomorrow: what does a weaver do with the alphabet?
last: THE DAY GOD COMES TO MIND.

lines: NO ONE'S BIRTH GETS THEM AHEAD.
cards: She passed. Barely, after a parallel park she won't describe, and with a laugh in the parking lot that her dad swears the whole DMV heard.

What Simran kept texting about afterward, though, was the line inside: a grandfather in a turban, a nurse in scrubs, a kid with a skateboard, a woman praying under her breath, everyone holding the same paper number.
Nobody's birth got them to the front. Kabir, the weaver, asked about exactly that, in Gauri, on Ang 324.

teach.b: Kabir's pages run from Ang 323 to 339, and on Ang 324 he puts a question to the proud, in paraphrase: in the womb there's no caste and no family line; all are made from the same divine seed.
If you're a Brahmin, born of a Brahmin mother, why didn't you arrive by some other way? How are you a Brahmin and I a Shudra?

teach.h: BLOOD IN ME, AND MILK IN YOU?
teach.b: Is there blood in me and milk in you? Kabir was a weaver, speaking into the caste pride of his own time and place. He isn't mocking anyone's faith.
He's asking a person to look at his own body.
And the answer is in the question: same birth, same blood. One human family, with no line to cut.
That's the day's word, lightly, and it lands right on the week. The letters, each one pointing past itself. Peace begins, in the pause.
Peace continues, like a lotus. Every day is his, whatever the moon. The daily routine, which ends in helping others.
Arjan's ballad: a day is beautiful when God comes to mind.
And today, the weaver's questions, which make a line at the DMV look a lot like the Granth.

how: Kabir's hymns stand in the Guru Granth Sahib beside the Gurus' own and are sung as kirtan; at the gurdwara everyone sits together on the floor for langar, whatever their birth.

games.q: a classmate says his family is "just better" because of who his great-grandparents were. what's Kabir's question to him?
o: is there blood in me and milk in you? no one is born above anyone.
Kabir would tell him to stop speaking to people like that.
Kabir says only weavers understand what birth means.
games.why: on Ang 324 Kabir asks the proud to look at their own birth: no caste in the womb, all from one seed, the same blood.

practice: Hold up your hands and look at them: the lines, the veins, the color of the blood just under the skin. Every hand you shook this week runs on the same. Breathe slowly, and let that be the whole thought.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: jaat, caste or birth-group; on Ang 324 Kabir says there is none in the womb.

carryVoice: Your line: the weaver's questions. Same birth, same blood, and the same line for everyone. Onward.
